messages:
anna_ml: heads-up — after quantizing the HF checkpoint and converting the tokenizer with our `hf->redwood` script, we see a consistent quality regression on the conversational evals (~3-4% drop). looks correlated with some tokens in non-ascii inputs. attaching quick repro below.

devon: can you paste a minimal repro (input + tokens from both sides)? also which tokenizer lib/version?

anna_ml: using `tokenizers` 0.15.3 + huggingface transformers 4.35.0. repro: input has composed and decomposed accents and a couple of nonbreaking spaces.

```
# input
s = "Alice\u00A0said: cafe\u0301 is open"
# HF tokenizer (original)
hf_tokens = ["▁Alice", "said", ":", "▁caf", "é", "▁is", "▁open"]
# Redwood-converted tokenizer (after our conversion script)
rd_tokens = ["▁Alice", "said", ":", "▁c", "a", "\u0301", "fe", "▁is", "▁open"]
```

anna_ml: that `\u0301` (combining acute) is being tokenized as a separate token after conversion. HF original had it normalized/merged.

sasha: hmm that screams normalization mismatch + byte-fallback behavior. if the HF tokenizer used NFC or a normalizer that composes diacritics, and our converted pre-tokenizer did byte-level fallback without normalizing, you'd see the combining mark split out. did our conversion preserve `normalizer` config?

anna_ml: looked at the exported `tokenizer.json` — `normalizer` field was missing in the converted file. our script drops the HF normalizer when it detects byte_fallback pretokenizer.

sasha: ok. quick fix: run `unicodedata.normalize('NFC', text)` before tokenization or set the tokenizer normalizer to NFC during conversion. small snippet: 

```
import unicodedata
text = "cafe\u0301"
unicodedata.normalize('NFC', text)  # -> 'café'
```

devon: also note whitespace handling: HF uses a prefix-space convention (`▁` or leading spaces) depending on model. our conversion switched from a `Whitespace` pre-tokenizer to a generic `ByteFallback` which strips the prefix marker in some cases, causing off-by-one token shifts for prompts that rely on leading-space semantics. that shifts logits for chat-turn boundaries.

eva: is this why some chat templates started failing? we saw system tokens like `<|system|>` being split unexpectedly in a canary run.

anna_ml: yes — special tokens mapping changed too. the conversion forgot to mark the chat delimiter tokens as `special_tokens` in the new tokenizer object, so the byte-level fallback treated them as normal text and split them.

sasha: action items: 1) update conversion to preserve `normalizer` (force NFC) 2) ensure special_tokens_map entries are preserved and re-registered 3) prefer `Whitespace` + `ByteFallback` combo that mirrors HF behavior rather than pure `ByteFallback` 4) add a small unit test in onboarding pipeline that tokenizes a set of hard unicode/whitespace edgecases and diffs token counts.

devon: adding: add an eval that compares token alignment for prompts (prefix tokens) — we should fail onboarding if tokenization shifts cause >1 token drift for a canonical prompt set.

infra-bot: deploy-canary: tokenizer-conversion-fix pushed to staging (job id: build-8921). running full tokenization-diff smoke test. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

anna_ml: thanks — once staging passes i'll re-run the quantized model evals. for reference, here's the small test set we used: `["Alice\u00A0said: cafe\u0301 is open", "Mix of \u00E9 and e\u0301", "leading space: ' hi' vs 'hi'"]` — those three catch most of the regressions.

sasha: optional: we might also add an explicit conversion flag `--force-normalizer=NFC` so model owners can opt-in if HF model used a custom normalizer.

anna_ml: agreed. will PR changes to the converter + add the tests. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
